text_blocks.snippet: Bupivacaine is a local anesthetic primarily used to numb specific areas of the body before or during surgical and medical procedures, as well as for managing postoperative pain. It works by blocking nerve signals that transmit pain, preventing the sensation of pain in the targeted area.
snippet_highlighted_words: to numb specific areas of the body before or during surgical and medical procedures, as well as for managing postoperative pain

list.title: Surgery:
list.snippet: Bupivacaine is commonly injected before or during various surgical procedures to numb the surgical site and surrounding tissues, reducing pain and discomfort.

list.title: Medical Procedures:
list.snippet: It can also be used for numbing specific areas before or during other medical procedures like dental work, injections, or biopsies.

list.title: Regional Anesthesia:
list.snippet: It's used to create regional nerve blocks, like brachial plexus or sciatic nerve blocks, which can numb a larger area of the body, such as an arm or leg, during surgery or for pain management.

list.title: Extended-Release Options:
list.snippet: Bupivacaine is available in formulations like liposome injection (Posimir) that provide pain relief for up to 72 hours after surgery, reducing the need for opioid painkillers, according to the Mayo Clinic.

list.title: Combination Therapies:
list.snippet: It may also be used in combination with other medications, like meloxicam, to manage pain after surgery, especially for soft tissue or muscle/bone surgeries.
Bupivacaine belongs to a class of medications called local anesthetics.
It works by blocking nerve signals, preventing them from transmitting pain messages to the brain.
This blockage occurs at the nerve endings, either locally at the injection site or through regional nerve blocks.

list.title: Administration:
list.snippet: Bupivacaine is typically administered by injection by a healthcare professional.

list.title: Safety:
list.snippet: It's crucial to have bupivacaine administered by a trained healthcare provider, as it can have serious side effects if not used correctly.

list.title: Special Precautions:
list.snippet: There are certain situations where bupivacaine may not be recommended, especially in high concentrations for epidural injections during pregnancy, according to MedlinePlus.

list.title: Other Uses:
list.snippet: Bupivacaine may have other uses as prescribed by a doctor.
